main_body: Hospital bed drawn from the front: a grey headboard/frame with vertical slats at the top, a white pillow and sheet, and a blue blanket, all stacked vertically. The mattress and sheet read as a front-facing panel.
top_band: none. The column starts with a pale grey frame band (rows ~11-12) and vertical bars (rows 13-19) that read as a headboard face. Rows 20-22 are a dark band, then the white sheet starts at row 23. There is no horizontal surface several rows tall.
evidence: Reading a single column down the middle, I meet the pale frame line at rows 11-12, then the slatted headboard bars at rows 13-19, a dark bar at rows 20-22, then white pillow and sheet, then a blue blanket and a white sheet to row ~44. The bed is stacked as vertical faces with no foreshortened mattress top. The pillow, sheet and blanket are seen face-on, as in a front elevation. The only top-like part is a 1-2 row frame line, which counts as a rim. No front edge line, no eave shadow, no inset front.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 4 lightness steps on the white and grey materials. The sheet is a large area of near-flat white with only a faint shadow. The blue blanket has 3 bands. The outline is a dark grey-blue column on the sides, close to neutral, with no clear tint from the adjacent material. There is no grain or texture dots, so the sheet and frame read as flat fills. Tile density is much lower than the stall and well references, which carry many colours per tile.
